title: john
description: John the Ripper (JtR) is an offline password cracker supporting hundreds of hash and cipher formats, with helper scripts to extract hashes from encrypted files (zip, PDF, SSH keys, and more).

Getting Started.Getting Started:
The community-maintained **"jumbo"** build is what almost everyone actually wants — the stock `john` core supports only about a dozen formats, while jumbo adds 470+. Current stable jumbo is **1.9.0-jumbo-1**; a rolling `bleeding-jumbo` development branch tracks ongoing work between releases.

## 1. Install

```bash
sudo pacman -S john
```

The Arch `extra` package builds the jumbo variant, so `john`, `zip2john`, `ssh2john`, `pdf2john`, and friends are all present after install.

## 2. Check the build

```bash
john --list=build-info
```

Confirms which optional features (OpenMP, GPU/OpenCL support via `--format=*-opencl`, etc.) your build includes.

## 3. First crack

```bash
unshadow /etc/passwd /etc/shadow > /tmp/combined.txt
john /tmp/combined.txt
```

Only meaningful against your own machine's hashes for a local audit — never run this against a shadow file you don't own. See [Legal Notes](/john/legal-notes/).
Getting Started.Cracking Modes:
John tries several modes in order by default; understanding them lets you target the right one instead of waiting through all of them.

## Single crack mode

```bash
john --single hashes.txt
```

Uses info from the hash file itself (usernames, GECOS fields) as candidate passwords with light mangling. Fast, and often the first hit for accounts using username-derived passwords.

## Wordlist mode

```bash
john --wordlist=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt --rules hashes.txt
```

`--rules` applies mangling rules (leet-speak substitutions, appended digits, capitalization variants) to every wordlist entry, massively expanding effective coverage without a bigger wordlist.

## Incremental (brute-force) mode

```bash
john --incremental hashes.txt
```

Tries all character combinations in an optimized order based on character frequency statistics. Only practical for short hashes or fast hash types — this is where GPU offload to Hashcat usually makes more sense for anything non-trivial.

## Showing cracked results

```bash
john --show hashes.txt
```
Getting Started.Extracting Hashes:
Jumbo ships dozens of `*2john` helper scripts that pull a crackable hash out of a protected file format.

## Common ones

| Script | Extracts from |
| --- | --- |
| `zip2john` | ZIP archives (classic + AES) |
| `rar2john` | RAR archives |
| `pdf2john` | Password-protected PDFs |
| `ssh2john` | Encrypted OpenSSH private keys |
| `keepass2john` | KeePass `.kdbx` databases |
| `office2john` | Office `.docx`/`.xlsx`/`.pptx` |

## Workflow

```bash
ssh2john id_rsa > id_rsa.hash
john --wordlist=rockyou.txt id_rsa.hash
john --show id_rsa.hash
```

This is also the standard hand-off point to Hashcat: extract with the `*2john` script, then feed the resulting hash line to `hashcat` if you want GPU-accelerated cracking instead — see the `hashcat` docs' [Attack Modes](/hashcat/attack-modes/) page.

Guides.Custom Rules:
Rules transform each wordlist candidate before it's tried, dramatically increasing hit rate against human-chosen passwords.

## Using a built-in rule set

```bash
john --wordlist=rockyou.txt --rules=Jumbo hashes.txt
```

`--rules=Jumbo` is the large bundled rule set; `--rules` alone uses the smaller default `Single` rules section.

## Writing a custom rule

Add a section to `~/.john/john.local.conf`:

```ini
[List.Rules:Custom]
c $[0-9] $[0-9]
l c $!
u $2 $0 $2 $6
```

Each line is one transformation: `c` capitalizes, `$X` appends `X`, `l` lowercases the whole word. Run with:

```bash
john --wordlist=rockyou.txt --rules=Custom hashes.txt
```

## Combining wordlist + mask

```bash
john --wordlist=rockyou.txt --rules --mask='^1?w?d?d' hashes.txt
```

Prepends `1` and appends two digits to every mangled wordlist candidate — useful for policies that force a digit and a leading/trailing character.

*Part of the [Extracting Hashes](/john/extracting-hashes/) page.* End-to-end script: extract a hash from a ZIP, crack it, print the result.

Source: `example/crack_zip.sh`

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ZIP="${1:?usage: crack_zip.sh <file.zip>}"

zip2john "$ZIP" > /tmp/zip.hash
john --wordlist=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt /tmp/zip.hash
john --show /tmp/zip.hash
```

Run it:

```bash
chmod +x example/crack_zip.sh
./example/crack_zip.sh secrets.zip
```

CLI Reference.john:
## Synopsis

```
john [options] [password-files]
```

## Common options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--single` | Single crack mode |
| `--wordlist=FILE` | Wordlist mode using `FILE` |
| `--rules[=NAME]` | Apply mangling rules (default or named section) |
| `--incremental[=MODE]` | Brute-force mode |
| `--mask=MASK` | Mask mode, e.g. `?l?l?l?l?d?d` |
| `--format=NAME` | Force a specific hash format |
| `--fork=N` | Fork `N` processes for CPU parallelism |
| `--show` | Show already-cracked passwords for a hash file |
| `--list=formats` | List every supported hash/cipher format |
| `--test` | Benchmark supported formats on this machine |
| `--session=NAME` | Name this run for later `--restore` |
| `--restore=NAME` | Resume a named interrupted session |

Full manual: `man john` (jumbo build) or the `doc/` directory bundled with the source.

Project.FAQ:
### `No password hashes loaded`

John couldn't auto-detect the format of the input, or every hash in the file is a format John doesn't support. Try forcing detection with `--format=` and a guess (`--list=formats` shows all options), or confirm the `*2john` extraction script actually produced valid output.

### Cracking is much slower than Hashcat for the same hash

Expected for GPU-friendly hash types (fast hashes like raw MD5/SHA1, NTLM). John is primarily CPU-based; Hashcat's GPU backends are typically orders of magnitude faster for those formats. John still wins for many "unusual" formats and file-based extractions Hashcat doesn't cover as completely (some legacy Unix crypt variants, certain archive formats).

### `--fork` vs OpenMP — which should I use?

Use `--fork=N` for hash formats without OpenMP support, or when you want hard process isolation. For OpenMP-enabled formats, John already threads automatically based on `OMP_NUM_THREADS` — check `--list=build-info` to see if your build has OpenMP.
